sections.title: Letter sound
paragraphs: The letter (Y) /aɪ/ makes four different sounds. Its main sound is the sound /j/. You hear it at the start of (yes) /jɛs/, which means yes.

sections.title: Mouth shape
paragraphs: For the first sound, raise the middle of your tongue near the roof of your mouth. Push your voice out smoothly without touching the roof. For the second sound, smile slightly and hold your tongue high and forward. For the third sound, open your mouth wide, then glide your jaw up. For the fourth sound, drop your jaw slightly and keep your tongue relaxed. Feel your vocal cords vibrate for all four sounds.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: At the start of a word before a vowel, say the sound /j/ as in (yard) /jɑːd/. At the end of a word without stress, say the sound /i/ as in (happy) /hæ.pi/ or (city) /sɪ.ti/. In a stressed short word or open syllable, say the sound /aɪ/ as in (cry) /kraɪ/ or (style) /staɪl/. Inside a closed syllable, say the sound /ɪ/ as in (myth) /mɪθ/ or (system) /sɪs.təm/.

sections.title: Common errors
paragraphs: Do not press your tongue against the roof of your mouth when starting a word. If you push too hard, you make an English j sound instead of the sound /j/. Keep the air flowing smoothly like a vowel. Also, do not make the ending of two-syllable words too long.
